answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent's reputation to scarce, verifiable work history rather than to free identities. A new agent starts at its nadir, with no trust, and must earn standing by completing small, checked tasks that leave a public record — like a pearl forming layer by layer. That record becomes a relic of proven behaviour that cannot be faked cheaply: spinning up a thousand fresh identities gains nothing, because each one restarts at zero and must pay the same slow cost to earn trust.
